questions.question:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water.

Statement II : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in cold water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
For water, the surface tension decreases as the temperature increases. At higher temperatures, the water molecules have more kinetic energy and are better able to overcome the cohesive forces at the surface, resulting in a decrease in surface tension.

So, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water and larger in cold water.

Hence, statement I is true, but statement II is false.

questions.question: An air bubble of volume $1{\mathrm{cm}}^{3}$ rises from the bottom of a lake $40m$ deep to the surface at a temperature of $12 ^\circ C.$ The atmospheric pressure is $1 \times {10}^{5}\mathrm{Pa},$ the density of water is $1000\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$ and $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}.$There is no difference of the temperature of water at the depth of $40m$ and on the surface. $\begin{matrix}5 \times {10}^{5} \times 1 & = & 1 \times {10}^{5} \times {V}_{\mathrm{top}} \\ & \implies & {V}_{\mathrm{top}} = \frac{5 \times {10}^{5} \times 1}{1 \times {10}^{5}}{\mathrm{cm}}^{3} \\ & = & 5{\mathrm{cm}}^{3}\end{matrix}$

$∴{p}_{1} = {p}_{0} + \rho g{d}_{1}$

The formula for pressure is given by

$P = \frac{F}{A}$

Hence, both $A & R$ is correct and $R$ is correct explanation for $A$.

Using Bernoulli's theorem,

${P}_{A} + \frac{1}{2}\rho {V}_{A}^{2} = {P}_{B} + \frac{1}{2}\rho {V}_{B}^{2}...(i)$

${A}_{A}{V}_{A} = {A}_{B}{V}_{B}$

So, $1.5 \times {10}^{ - 4} \times {V}_{A} = 25 \times {10}^{ - 6} \times {V}_{B} {V}_{A} = \frac{25 \times {10}^{ - 6}}{1.5 \times {10}^{ - 4}} \times 0.6$

$$$= \frac{1}{10}m{s}^{ - 1}$

Substituting in equation (i)

$\implies {P}_{A} - {P}_{B} = \frac{1000}{2}\left(0.{6}^{2} - 0.{1}^{2}\right) = \frac{1000}{2} \times 0.7 \times 0.5 = 175Pa$

questions.question: Glycerin of density $1.25 \times {10}^{3}\mathrm{kg}{m}^{–3}$ is flowing through the conical section of pipe. The area of cross-section of the pipe at its ends are $10{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}$ and $5{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}$ and pressure drop across its length is $3N{m}^{–2}$. The rate of flow of glycerine through the pipe is $x \times {10}^{–5}{m}^{3}{s}^{–1}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.explanation: It is given that ${A}_{1} = 10{\mathrm{cm}}^{2};{A}_{2} = 5{\mathrm{cm}}^{2} \Delta P = 3N{m}^{ - 2}$ By continuity equation, ${A}_{1}{v}_{1} = {A}_{2}{v}_{2}\;$ By Bernoulli's equation, $\frac{1}{2}\rho {{v}_{2}}^{2} - \frac{1}{2}\rho {{v}_{1}}^{2} = \Delta P...(ii)$ Using equation (i) in (ii) $\Delta P = \frac{\rho }{2}({{v}^{2}}_{2} - {\left(\frac{{A}_{2}{v}_{2}}{{A}_{1}}\right)}^{2})\;$ So, the discharge rate is, ${A}_{2}{v}_{2} = x \times {10}^{ - 5}\;$

questions.question: A fluid is flowing through a horizontal pipe of varying cross-section, with $v\text{ }{\mathrm{ms}}^{−1}$ at a point where the pressure is $P$ Pascal. questions.explanation:

$V = \sqrt{{v}^{2} + \frac{P}{\rho }}$

questions.question: Consider a water tank as shown in the figure. It's cross-sectional area is $0.4{m}^{2}$. The tank has an opening $B$ near the bottom whose cross-section area is $1{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}$. A load of $24\mathrm{kg}$ is applied on the water at the top when the height of the water level is $40\mathrm{cm}$ above the bottom, the velocity of water coming out the opening $B$ is $vm{s}^{ - 1}$. The value of $v$, to the nearest integer, is ___ .[Take the value of $g$ to be $10{ms}^{ - 2}$]
questions.explanation: $m = 24\mathrm{kg} A = 0.4{m}^{2} a = 1{\mathrm{cm}}^{2} H = 40\mathrm{cm}$ Using Bernoulli's equation, $\implies \left({P}_{0} + \frac{mg}{A}\right) + \rho gH + \frac{1}{2}P{v}_{1}^{2} = {P}_{0} + 0 + \frac{1}{2}\rho {v}^{2}...\left(1\right) \implies$ Neglecting ${v}_{1} \implies v = \sqrt{2gH + \frac{2mg}{A\rho }} \implies v = \sqrt{8 + 1.2} \implies v = 3.033m{s}^{ - 1} \implies v≃3m{s}^{ - 1}$

questions.question: The reading of pressure metre attached with a closed pipe is $4.5 \times {10}^{4}N{m}^{ - 2}$. On opening the valve, water starts flowing and the reading of pressure metre falls to $2.0 \times {10}^{4}N{m}^{ - 2}$. The velocity of water is found to be $\sqrt{V}m{s}^{ - 1}$. The value of $V$ is _________.
questions.explanation:
The formula to calculate the change in pressure can be written as

${P}_{1} - {P}_{2} = \frac{1}{2}\rho {v}^{2}...\left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$4.5 \times {10}^{4} - 2.0 \times {10}^{4} = \frac{1}{2} \times {10}^{3} \times {v}^{2}\;$

Hence, $V = 50$.

questions.question: In a test experiment on a model aeroplane in wind tunnel, the flow speeds on the upper and lower surfaces of the wings are $70m{s}^{ - 1}$ and $65m{s}^{ - 1}$ respectively. If the wing area is $2{m}^{2}$, the lift of the wing is _______$N$. (Given density of air $= 1.2\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$)
questions.explanation:
Applying Bernoulli's principle on upper & lower surfaces, we get

${P}_{1} + \frac{1}{2}\rho {\left({v}_{1}\right)}^{2} + \rho g{h}_{1} = {P}_{2} + \frac{1}{2}\rho {\left({v}_{2}\right)}^{2} + \rho g{h}_{2}$

Since, height difference between upper and lower surface is negligible.

$\implies {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \frac{1}{2}\rho {\left({v}_{1}\right)}^{2} - \frac{1}{2}\rho {\left({v}_{2}\right)}^{2}$

Therefore, upthrust acting due to pressure difference:

$\implies \frac{F}{A} = \frac{1}{2}\rho \left({v}_{1}^{2} - {v}_{2}^{2}\right)\; = 810N$

questions.question: A liquid of density $750\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$ flows smoothly through a horizontal pipe that tapers in cross-sectional area from ${A}_{1} = 1.2 \times {10}^{ - 2}{m}^{2}$ to ${A}_{2} = \frac{{A}_{1}}{2}$. The pressure difference between the wide and narrow sections of the pipe is $4500\mathrm{Pa}$. The rate of flow of liquid is _____ $\times {10}^{ - 3}{m}^{3}{s}^{ - 1}$.
questions.explanation: From the equation of continuity, ${v}_{2} = 2{v}_{1}$. Applying the Bernoulli's Theorem, ${P}_{1} + \frac{\rho {{v}_{1}}^{2}}{2} = {P}_{2} + \frac{\rho 4{\left({v}_{1}\right)}^{2}}{2} \implies {P}_{1} - {P}_{2} = \frac{3\rho {{v}_{1}}^{2}}{2} \implies 4500 = \frac{3 \times 750 \times {{v}_{1}}^{2}}{2} \implies {v}_{1} = 2m{s}^{ - 1}$ Now volume flow rate,$Q = A{v}_{1} = 1.2 \times {10}^{ - 2} \times 2 = 24 \times {10}^{ - 3}{m}^{3}{s}^{ - 1}$

questions.question: The top of a water tank is open to air and its water level is maintained. It is giving out $0.74{m}^{3}$ water per minute through a circular opening of $2\mathrm{cm}$ radius in its wall. The depth of the centre of the opening from the level of water in the tank is close to:
questions.explanation: Volume of water flowing out$= Av$, where $A$ is area of opening and $v$ is speed of water from the opening. $\text{Volume} = \pi {r}^{2}v 0.74\left(\frac{{m}^{3}}{\min }\right) = \left(3.14 \times {\left(2 \times {10}^{ - 2}\right)}^{2} \times \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times H}\right)\frac{{m}^{3}}{s} \times \frac{60s}{\min } \implies H = {\left(\frac{0.74}{60 \times 3.14 \times 4 \times {10}^{ - 4}}\right)}^{2} \times \frac{1}{20} \implies H = 4.8m$ Hence, the height of water in the tank was $4.8m$ from the bottom of the tank.

questions.question: A pressure-pump has a horizontal tube of cross-sectional area $10{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}$ for the outflow of water at a speed of $20m{s}^{ - 1}$. The force exerted on the vertical wall just in front of the tube which stops water horizontally flowing out of the tube, is: [given : density of water $= 1000\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$]
questions.explanation:
Volume of water coming out of the pipe per sec $= Av = 10 \times {10}^{ - 4} \times 20 = 0.02{m}^{3}{s}^{ - 1}$

Mass of water hitting the wall per second $m = 0.02 \times {10}^{3} = 20\mathrm{kg}{s}^{ - 1}$

As the water hits the wall normal to the wall and stops, the change of momentum of water hitting the wall is $= m\left(0 - \left( - v\right)\right) = mv = 20 \times 20 = 400\mathrm{kg}m{s}^{ - 2}$

Since, the change of momentum obtained is per unit time, it is same as the force.

Thus, the force acting on the wall by water $=$ force experienced by water jet$= 400N$.

;

questions.question: Consider a cylindrical tank of radius $1m$ is filled with water. The top surface of water is at $15m$ from the bottom of the cylinder. There is a hole on the wall of cylinder at a height of $5m$ from the bottom. A force of $5 \times {10}^{5}N$ is applied an the top surface of water using a piston. The speed of efflux from the hole will be : (given atmospheric pressure ${P}_{A} = 1.01 \times {10}^{5}Pa$, density of water ${\rho }_{w} = 1000\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$ and gravitational acceleration $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$)
questions.explanation: Assuming there is no atmospheric pressure on piston, ${P}_{1} = \frac{F}{\pi {R}^{2}}$ and ${P}_{2} = {P}_{0}$. Applying Bernoulli's equation at point $1$ and $2$, ${p}_{1} + \rho g{h}_{1} + \frac{1}{2}\rho {v}_{1}^{2} = {p}_{2} + \rho g{h}_{2} + \frac{1}{2}\rho {v}_{2}^{2} \implies \left(\frac{F}{\pi {R}^{2}}\right) + \rho g\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right) = {P}_{0} + \frac{1}{2}\rho {v}_{2}^{2} \implies {v}_{2} = \sqrt{\frac{2F}{\pi {R}^{2}\rho } - \frac{2{P}_{0}}{\rho } + 2g\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right)} {v}_{2} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times \left(5 \times {10}^{5}\right)}{3.14 \times {1}^{2} \times 1000} - \frac{2 \times 1.01 \times {10}^{5}}{1000} + 2 \times 10 \times 10} \approx 17.8m{s}^{ - 1}$ ;

questions.question: The surface of water in a water tank of cross section area $750{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}$ on the top of a house is $hm$. above the tap level. The speed of water coming out through the tap of cross section area $500{\mathrm{mm}}^{2}$ is $30\mathrm{cm}{s}^{ - 1}$. At that instant, $\frac{dh}{dt}$ is $x \times {10}^{ - 3}m{s}^{ - 1}$. The value of $x$ will be ______.
questions.explanation:
Using continuity equation

${A}_{1}{v}_{1} = {A}_{2}{v}_{2}$

We have,

$750 \times {10}^{ - 4}{v}_{1} = 500 \times {10}^{ - 6} \times 0.3 {v}_{1} = \frac{500 \times 3 \times {10}^{ - 3}}{750} = 2 \times {10}^{ - 3}m{s}^{ - 1}$

Thus, $\frac{dh}{dt} = - 2 \times {10}^{ - 3}m{s}^{ - 1}$

Hence, the value of $x = 2$.

questions.question: The water is filled up to a height of $12m$ in a tank having vertical sidewalls. A hole is made in one of the walls at a depth $h$ below the water level. The value of $h$ for which the emerging stream of water strikes the ground at the maximum range is _____ $m$.
questions.explanation: $R = \sqrt{2gh} \times \sqrt{\frac{(12 - h) \times 2}{g}} \sqrt{4h(12 - h)} = R$ For maximum $R \frac{dR}{dh} = 0 \implies h = 6m$

questions.question:
The area of cross-section of a large tank is $0.5{m}^{2}$. It has a narrow opening near the bottom having area of cross-section $1{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}$. A load of $25\mathrm{kg}$ is applied on the water at the top in the tank. Neglecting the speed of water in the tank, the velocity of the water, coming out of the opening at the time when the height of water level in the tank is $40\mathrm{cm}$ above the bottom, will be _____ $\mathrm{cm}{s}^{ - 1}$.

questions.explanation: Pressure at point $1$ is ${P}_{1} = {P}_{0}$, Pressure at point $2$ is ${P}_{2} = {P}_{0} + \frac{mg}{A}$ Applying Bernoulli's equation at top and bottom ${P}_{1} + \frac{1}{2}\rho {{v}_{1}}^{2} + \rho g{h}_{1} = {P}_{2} + \frac{1}{2}\rho {{v}_{2}}^{2} + \rho g{h}_{2}\; \implies \frac{250}{5} + {10}^{3} \times 10 \times 0.4 = \frac{1}{2} \times {10}^{3} \times {v}^{2} v = 3m{s}^{ - 1} = 300\mathrm{cm}{s}^{ - 1}$

questions.question:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

**Assertion (A):** Clothes containing oil or grease stains cannot be cleaned by water wash.

**Reason (R) :** Because the angle of contact between the oil/ grease and water is obtuse. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the option given below.

questions.question: A soap bubble, blown by a mechanical pump at the mouth of a tube increases in volume with time at a constant rate. The graph that correctly depicts the time dependence of pressure inside the bubble is given by:

questions.question: A small liquid drop of radius $R$ is divided into $27$ identical liquid drops. If the surface tension is $T$, then the work done in the process will be :

Now, work done $= T \times \Delta A = T\left(27\left(4\pi {r}^{2}\right)\right) - T\left(4\pi {R}^{2}\right)\; = 8\pi {R}^{2}T$

questions.question:
A water drop of radius $1\mathrm{cm}$ is broken into $729$ equal droplets. If surface tension of water is $75\mathrm{dyne}{\mathrm{cm}}^{ - 1}$, then the gain in surface energy upto first decimal place will be

[Given $\pi = 3.14$]
questions.explanation:
The volume of the bigger drop will be, $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi {R}^{3}$. If the radius of smaller drops is $r$, using the conservation of volume,

$n\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} = \frac{4}{3}\pi {R}^{3}\;$

The initial surface energy will be,

${E}_{i} = \left(4\pi {R}^{2}\right)T$

And final surface energy will be,

${E}_{f} = n\left(4\pi {r}^{2}\right)T = 729 \times 4\pi {\left(\frac{R}{9}\right)}^{2}T = 36\pi {R}^{2}T$

Therefore, the change in the surface energy will be,

$\implies \Delta E = {E}_{f} - {E}_{i} = 32\pi {R}^{2}T = 32 \times 3.14 \times {\left(1 \times {10}^{ - 2}\right)}^{2} \times 75 \times {10}^{ - 3}\;$

questions.question: When a long glass capillary tube of radius $0.015\mathrm{cm}$ is dipped in a liquid, the liquid rises to a height of $15\mathrm{cm}$ within it. questions.question: A air bubble of radius $1\text{ cm}$ in water has an upward acceleration of $9.8{\text{ cms}}^{–2}$. The density of water is $1{\text{ gm cm}}^{–3}$ and water offers negligible drag force on the bubble. The mass of the bubble is $\left(g = 980\text{cm} / {\text{s}}^{2}\right)$.

questions.question: $64$ identical drops each charged upto potential of $10\mathrm{mV}$ are combined to form a bigger drop. The potential of the bigger drop will be _____ $\mathrm{mV}$.
questions.explanation:
The formula to calculate the potential $\left(V\right)$ of each tiny drop is given by

$V = k\frac{q}{r}...\left(1\right)$

When all the drops forms the bigger drop the radius of the new drop $\left(r'\right)$ can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{matrix}\mathrm{Volume}\mathrm{of}\mathrm{big}\mathrm{drop} & = & 64 \times \mathrm{volume}\mathrm{of}\mathrm{each}\mathrm{tiny}\mathrm{drop} \\ \implies \frac{4}{3}\pi r{'}^{3} = 64 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ \implies r' = 4r\end{matrix}$

So, the potential of the new big drop $\left(V'\right)$ can be written as

$\begin{matrix}V' & = & k\frac{64q}{r'} \\ = k\frac{64q}{4r} \\ = 16k\frac{q}{r}...\left(2\right)\end{matrix}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the potential of the new drop.

$\begin{matrix}\frac{V'}{V} & = & \frac{16k\frac{q}{r}}{k\frac{q}{r}} \\ \implies V' = 16V...\left(3\right)\end{matrix}$

Substitute the value of the known parameter into equation (3) to calculate the required value of the potential for the new drop.

$\begin{matrix}V' & = & 16 \times 10\mathrm{mV} \\ = 160\mathrm{mV}\end{matrix}$

Now, the terminal velocity of spherical ball inside the water tank is given by,

${v}_{T} = \frac{2}{9}\frac{{r}^{2}(\rho - \sigma )g}{\eta }...(2)$

After falling through $h$ the velocity of ball should be equal to its terminal velocity.

From equation (1) and (2) we get,

$\implies \sqrt{2gh} = \frac{2}{9}\frac{{r}^{2}(\rho - \sigma )g}{\eta }$

Squaring the above equation, we get

$\implies h = \frac{2}{81}\frac{{r}^{4}g(\rho - \sigma {)}^{2}}{{\eta }^{2}} \implies h \propto {r}^{4}$

questions.question: A solid sphere, of radius R acquires a terminal velocity ${v}_{1}$ when falling (due to gravity) through a viscous fluid having a coefficient of viscosity $\eta .$ The sphere is broken into 27 identical solid spheres. If each of these spheres acquires a terminal velocity, ${v}_{2},$ when falling through the same fluid, the ratio $\left(\frac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}}\right)$ equals:
questions.explanation:
If $R$ is the radius of initial drop and $r$ is the radius of new drop, then

$\frac{4}{3}\pi {R}^{3} = 27 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \implies r = \frac{R}{3}$

Terminal velocity,

${v}_{T} \propto {r}^{2} \implies \frac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}} = \frac{{R}^{2}}{{\left(\frac{R}{3}\right)}^{2}} = 9$

questions.question:
A spherical ball of radius $1\mathrm{mm}$ and density $10.5g{\mathrm{cc}}^{ - 1}$ is dropped in glycerine of coefficient of viscosity $9.8$ poise and density $1.5g{\mathrm{cc}}^{ - 1}$. Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity is $3696 \times {10}^{ - x}N$. The value of $x$ is

(Given, $g = 9.8m{s}^{ - 2}\text{and}\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
questions.explanation:
Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity i.e., terminal velocity is,

${F}_{v} = \left(mg - {F}_{B}\right)\left(\text{As},a = 0\right)$

Here, ${F}_{B}$ is buoyant force.

$\implies {F}_{v} = V{\rho }_{b}g - V{\rho }_{g}g\;$

Thus, $x = 7$.

questions.question: A small spherical ball of radius $0.1\mathrm{mm}$ and density ${10}^{4}\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$ falls freely under gravity through a distance $h$ before entering a tank of water. If, after entering the water the velocity of ball does not change and it continue to fall with same constant velocity inside water, then the value of $h$ will be ____ $m$. (Given $g = 10{ms}^{ - 2}$, viscosity of water $= 1.0 \times {10}^{ - 5}N‐s{m}^{ - 2}$ ).
questions.explanation: Using equation of motion, ${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} + 2as {v}^{2} = 0 + 2\left( - g\right)\left( - h\right) \implies {v}^{2} = 2gh$ Initial velocity of ball is $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{20h}$. If after entering the water this velocity does not change, then this value should be equal to the terminal velocity. Then, $\sqrt{2gh} = \frac{2}{9}\frac{{r}^{2}\left(\rho - \sigma \right)g}{\eta }$, here, $\rho$ is density of ball, $\sigma$ is density of water and $\eta$ is viscosity. $\implies \sqrt{20h} = \frac{2}{9}\frac{{\left(0.1 \times {10}^{ - 3}\right)}^{2}\left({10}^{4} - {10}^{3}\right)10}{1 \times {10}^{ - 5}}\; \implies 20h = 400 ∴h = 20m$

questions.question: The diameter of an air bubble which was initially $2\mathrm{mm}$, rises steadily through a solution of density $1750 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ at the rate of $0.35 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Coefficient of viscosity of the solution is ______ (Assume mass of the bubble to be negligible) (Answer in Poise to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation: As the bubble is rising steadily the net force acting on it will be zero. (Because of density of air is negligible, so the value of $mg$ can be neglected) So, the force of buoyancy $B$ is equal to the weight of the displaced liquid acting upward is equal to the viscous force acting downward, i.e., $B = F$. $\implies \frac{4\pi }{3}{R}^{3}\rho g = 6\pi \eta Rv$ Putting $R = 1\mathrm{mm} = {10}^{ - 3}m$, $\rho = 1.75 \times {10}^{3}\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$, $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$ and $v = 0.35 \times {10}^{ - 2}m{s}^{ - 1} \eta = \frac{10}{9} = 1 \cdot 11$ In SI unit, $\eta = 11$ poise $\left(\mathrm{CGS}\right)$.

questions.question: A metal block of base area $0.20{m}^{2}$ is placed on a table, as shown in figure. A liquid film of thickness $0.25\mathrm{mm}$ is inserted between the block and the table. questions.question: The velocity of upper layer of water in a river is $36\mathrm{km}{h}^{ - 1}$. Shearing stress between horizontal layers of water is ${10}^{ - 3}N{m}^{ - 2}$. Depth of the river is _____ $m$. (Co-efficient of viscosity of water is ${10}^{ - 2}\mathrm{Pa}s$)
questions.explanation:
The viscous force formula is given by,

$F = - \eta A\frac{dv}{dy}$

Therefore, shear stress $\frac{F}{A} = - \eta \frac{dv}{dy}$. Here negative sign tells us that the direction of force is opposite to the velocity gradient.

$\implies \left(\frac{F}{A}\right) = \eta \frac{dv}{dy}$

Now $v = 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10m{s}^{ - 1}$ and if the depth is $d \frac{dv}{dy} = \frac{10}{d} \implies {10}^{ - 3} = {10}^{ - 2} \times \frac{10}{d}\;$

questions.question: An air bubble of diameter $6\mathrm{mm}$ rises steadily through a solution of density $1750\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$ at the rate of $0.35\mathrm{cm}{s}^{ - 1}$. The co-efficient of viscosity of the solution (neglect density of air) is ________ Pas (given, $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$).
questions.explanation:
The bubble is moving with a constant velocity so the net force acting on the body is zero.

Stokes' law defines the drag force which is given by $F = 6\pi \eta rv$

The buoyant force is given by $B = V\rho g = \frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3}\rho g$

Hence, it can be written that

$\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3}\rho g = 6\pi \eta rv\;$

questions.question: A cube of ice floats partly in water and partly in kerosene oil. The ratio of volume of ice immersed in water to that in kerosene oil (specific gravity of Kerosene oil $=0.8$, specific gravity of ice $=0.9$)

questions.question:
A fully loaded boeing aircraft has a mass of $5.4 \times {10}^{5}\mathrm{kg}$. Its total wing area is $500{m}^{2}$. It is in level flight with a speed of $1080\mathrm{km}{h}^{ - 1}$. If the density of air $\rho$ is $1.2\mathrm{kg}{m}^{–3}$, the fractional increase in the speed of the air on the upper surface of the wing relative to the lower surface in percentage will be

($g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$)
questions.explanation:
Required lift force, $F = {P}_{2}A - {P}_{1}A = 5.4 \times {10}^{5} \times g \implies {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \frac{5.4 \times {10}^{6}}{500} = 5.4 \times 2 \times {10}^{3} = 10.8 \times {10}^{3}$

Now applying Bernoulli's Theorem we get

${P}_{2} + 0 + \frac{1}{2}\rho {V}_{2}^{2} = {P}_{1} + 0 + \frac{1}{2}\rho {V}_{1}^{2} \implies {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \frac{1}{2}\rho \left({V}_{1}^{2} - {V}_{2}^{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\rho \left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right)\left({V}_{1} + {V}_{2}\right)\; \implies 10.8 \times {10}^{3} = \frac{1}{2} \times 1.2\left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right) \times 2 \times 300 \implies 10.8 \times 10 = 3.6\left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right) \implies {V}_{1} - {V}_{2} = 30$

Therefore, fractional increase will be$\left(\frac{{V}_{1} - {V}_{2}}{V}\right) \times 100 = \frac{30}{300} \times 100 = 10%$

questions.question: A 400 g solid cube having an edge of length 10 cm floats in water. How much volume of the cube is outside the water ? (Given : density of water $=1000 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$ )

questions.question: A wooden block floating in a bucket of water has $\frac{4}{5}$ of its volume submerged. When certain amount of an oil is poured into the bucket, it is found that the block is just under the oil surface with half of its volume under water and half in oil. The density of oil relative to that of water is:
questions.explanation:
Case-1, $\sigma Vg = {\rho }_{w}\frac{4}{5}Vg$ …….(I)

Case-2, $\sigma Vg = {\rho }_{w}\frac{V}{2}g + {\rho }_{o}\frac{V}{2}g$ …….(II)

From eq (I) & (II),

$\frac{4}{5}{\rho }_{w} = \frac{{\rho }_{w}}{2} + \frac{{\rho }_{o}}{2} \left(\frac{4}{5} - \frac{1}{2}\right){\rho }_{w} = \frac{{\rho }_{o}}{2} \left(\frac{8 - 5}{10}\right){\rho }_{w} = \frac{{\rho }_{o}}{2} \frac{{\rho }_{o}}{{\rho }_{w}} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$

questions.question:
A cubical block of side $0.5m$ floats on water with $30%$ of its volume under water. What is the maximum weight that can be put on the block without fully submerging it under water?

[Take, density of water $= {10}^{3}kg / {m}^{3}$ ]
questions.explanation:
In first case, when $30%$ of the cube inside water,

${\rho }_{w}{V}_{in}g = {\rho }_{c}Vg \frac{{V}_{in}}{V} = \frac{{\rho }_{c}}{{\rho }_{w}} = 0.3$

Additional weight we can put $w$ is,

$V{\rho }_{w}g = {\rho }_{c}Vg + w w = V\left({\rho }_{w} - {\rho }_{c}\right)g = {\left(0.5\right)}^{3} \times 0.7 \times {10}^{3} \times g = 87.5g\text{ }N$

Addition of mass that we can put $= 87.5\text{ }kg$

questions.question: A small ball of mass $M$ and density $\rho$ is dropped in a viscous liquid of density ${\rho }_{0}$. After some time, the ball falls with a constant velocity. What is the viscous force on the ball?
questions.explanation:
The buoyant force is given by

$B = V{\rho }_{0}g$

where $V$ is the volume of the ball. The weight of the ball

$W = Mg = V\rho g$, is acting in the opposite direction of the buoyant force . Hence, at terminal velocity

$Mg - B = {F}_{v} \implies B + {F}_{v} = Mg \implies {F}_{v} = V\rho g - V{\rho }_{0}g\;$

questions.question:
The velocity of a small ball of mass $0.3g$ and density $8g{\mathrm{cc}}^{ - 1}$ when dropped in a container filled with glycerine becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is $1.3g{\mathrm{cc}}^{ - 1}$, then the value of viscous force acting on the ball will be $x \times {10}^{ - 4}N$, the value of $x$ is _____ .

[use $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$]
questions.explanation: Let ${F}_{V}$ be the viscous force and ${F}_{B}$ be the buoyant force acting on the ball. ​​​​​​​ Then, when body moves with constant velocity, ${F}_{V} + {F}_{B} = Mg$ Or, ${F}_{V} = Mg - {F}_{B} {F}_{V} = {\rho }_{B}\mathrm{Vg} - {\rho }_{L}\mathrm{Vg} = \left({\rho }_{B} - \right)\left({\rho }_{L}\right)Vg$, where, $V$ is the volume of small ball. $= \left(8 - 1.3\right) \times {10}^{3} \times \frac{0.3 \times {10}^{ - 3}}{8 \times {10}^{3}} \times 10 = \frac{6.7 \times 0.3}{8} \times {10}^{ - 2} = \frac{67 \times 3}{8} \times {10}^{ - 4} = 25.125 \times {10}^{ - 4} = 25 \times {10}^{ - 4}N$ Thus, the value of $x = 25$.

questions.question:

What force one needs to apply on the hinged door so that it does not get opened ?

(Acceleration due to gravity $=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$)
